category_notes.text: Read visual-style, restoration and perceptual-image research pages. New brushstroke guides distinguish learned painting from conventional palette math; the palette integration clearly identifies the separate image generator.

Read WanMove and OpenFilm primary descriptions and completed a Nuzky editing guide. Preview playback, an editable timeline and a successful export are separate checks; no renderer was run. Newly screened Framefields and openvidstudio expose concrete agent-driven rendering/capture workflows; their external model and renderer terms remain separate.

Read Neutone host/SDK information and GitLab audio-model integrations. Completed music-production, stem-separation and agent-authored sound guides, distinguishing neural synthesis from conventional instrument rendering.
Read neural surface/dynamics and scene-representation research. Completed GaussianGPT scene-generation and splat-segment object-isolation guides, with CUDA and model/data limits explicit.

Read NodeTool and OpenFilm contexts and reviewed OpenViz, Lightheart and OpenCalque. Browser access does not establish offline generation or native GPU support; script-shell pages supplied no runtime evidence.
Read Meta immersive-web and Google XR Blocks prototyping materials. Agent-created XR scenes still require actual device and interaction testing; no headset or deployment was tested.

Read neural collage and compression research, then completed learned painting and interactive style-exploration guides. Conventional color naming and simulation are distinguished from model inference.

Read Timeflux and physiological interaction contexts and completed AETHER gesture visuals. MediaPipe hand estimation, particle rendering and optional LLM assistance are distinct stages. Model-card follow-up found EdenLive video rendering for engine-driven interactive scenes; software is Apache-2.0 but DINOv3 and optional non-commercial FLUX components retain separate terms.
Read text-to-CAD and procedural design context, then inspected additional agent/CAD candidates from the retained catalog. Mesh or STEP export is not dimensional or manufacturing validation.
Read Cambrian engine and scene-generation descriptions. Completed Roqer agent editing and sound workflows while documenting proprietary Roblox and separate model/service dependencies.

Read learned dance and geometry-conditioned motion research and followed additional motion-capture candidates. A motion file or pose estimator does not establish reliable retargeting for a specific rig.

Completed the OpenSpline live-portrait guide and reviewed OmniShow multimodal human-object video code. Cloud demos and available base models are not substitutes for a released task-specific checkpoint.

Read Lumen and the SyncLight model card and completed TRHM relighting and Gaussian object-isolation guides. The SyncLight project site failed TLS verification; the readable model card is cited separately.
Read neural acoustic fields, sound simulation and OpenFollow documentation. Spatial sound/control suitability remains hardware-, geometry- and calibration-dependent.
Read event-to-video and lensless imaging research. LenslessMic now has a guide for provided measurements versus physical acquisition; no camera or optical mask was installed.
Completed source-based guides for Nuzky, pedit, OpenDub and Stem Studio. Editing controls, learned processing and local/cloud execution are identified separately.
Read VFIG and MuseDraw primary examples and reviewed plan-editor exports. A visually plausible raster preview does not establish editable vector structure or factual accuracy.

Read the modal typography page, which still describes forthcoming code. Existing font/calligraphy candidates remain under review where checkpoints, fonts or a reproducible generation entrypoint are unclear.
Read OpenFilm and completed Lightheart scene/script assistance and OpenDub translation/dubbing guides. Story continuity, speech timing and identity permissions need project-specific review.

Read Open Presentation export and agent-skill documentation. Format conversion has documented fidelity limits; current open tooling does not imply every PowerPoint feature round-trips correctly. The Vietnamese 2Anh distribution is retained for its documented localized extensions; the unchanged parent is not counted again. YominPost was screened for AI-assisted drafting; its default template driver is non-AI and some social connectors, including TikTok, are simulated.
Read LocalSR, lensless imaging and the SyncLight model card, and completed learned painting/compression guides. Inferred color or texture is not faithful photographic restoration.
Read the QGIS AI Agent registry and VFIG/MuseDraw contexts. Additional chart/graphics candidates were source-screened; coordinate systems and factual chart interpretation remain separate checks.

Read Ghost Arcade, Timeflux and stage-tracking descriptions and completed gesture-driven browser visuals. No projector calibration, visitor interaction or long-running installation test was performed. Phrame was screened for conversation-driven image displays; browser transcription and hosted models have distinct data-processing terms.
Read Neutone host/SDK and stage-tracking context. Completed audio and interactive-media guides; low-latency claims and device reliability were not accepted without independent evidence.

Read the German INTEX material-recommendation case study, including its design-stage material selection approach. No new fully reviewed garment-design application was established by that case study alone.

Reviewed vocal-annotation documentation and completed local dubbing and speech-tool guides. Translation, captions and synthesized speech require human review; a supported language is not an accuracy guarantee.

Read the SDAI F-Droid listing and reviewed Android typography and camera/sensor candidates. Android local generation, iOS remote services and browser interfaces have different requirements. The iSky source guide documents Xcode/iOS setup and an explicit blocker: five required Core ML style models are not distributed in the repository.
Read Pixels2GenAI and MIT RAISE Playground. Non-commercial educational materials are not silently classified as open-source software, and an educational demo does not prove a reusable application.

Read PyPottery and inverse-halftoning research and reviewed the Deep Halftoning implementation. Its README explicitly says paper numbers are not currently reproducible, so it is not promoted to a validated restoration route.

Expanded the effective plan with neural brushstroke painting and AI color direction before collection. Scent, haptics, caustics and paper-folding research remain in scope even when no eligible new app is established.
Read HapticGen’s text-conditioned vibration research and reported study. No new haptic device or independently tested application was established by this bounded pass.
Read neural acoustic fields and SoundSpaces descriptions. Geometry-based simulation is separated from learned inference, and no room/acoustic calibration was performed.

Read OpenFilm/NodeTool and completed Lightheart, Soundroo and related workflows. Agents can create structured media projects, but model accounts, execution permissions and service costs are additional dependencies.
Read the modal typography method and forthcoming-code notice. A research animation is not treated as a released, licensed, runnable typography application.
Read Learning2Dance and semantic/geometric motion research and screened additional capture/retargeting metadata. No generated choreography was validated with performers or a production rig.
Read COrigami folding and textile material-selection research. Learned aesthetic planning does not establish physical foldability, material durability or safe fabrication.
Read BinaryMuseGAN and completed KomaVision’s editable Turkish microtonal score workflow. Its model-training data/weight terms remain distinct from the Apache-licensed application.
Completed TRHM’s model/data/environment guide and read Lumen/SyncLight evidence. Dataset size and reported experiment GPUs are stated separately from undocumented minimum inference requirements.
Read Anemoia’s photo-to-fragrance installation and the updated AromaGen abstract. These are relevant creative AI findings, but a complete new open-source software release was not established.
Read InstructScene, Procedura and GardenDesigner and completed OpenCalque’s assistant/plan-editor guide. Scene generation and editable drawings are not engineering or construction approval.

Read DirectL and neural point light fields, and followed NeRC caustics research into its repository. NeRC currently contains only README/license and promises code later; no implementation is featured.
Read contextual human-motion and tracking descriptions. Foton’s page returned only a title, so it supplied no new implementation evidence for an AI puppetry workflow.

Read PyPottery and inspected the existing ceramic GAN candidate’s actual scripts. Training code exists, but the simple main script emits random arrays and training references local checkpoint paths; a reproducible creator guide remains pending.

Read text-to-CAD and Procedura context and inspected further agent-driven CAD candidates. Parametric model editing is distinguished from proven dimensional tolerances and print readiness. A text-to-3D model card led to constraint-kit, whose constrained AI program feeds CAD and mate solvers; geometric output still requires independent fabrication/engineering validation.
Read QGIS AI Agent’s visible plan/apply workflow and model-data disclosure. No user map or private geospatial data was transmitted during this source review.
Read FRIDA’s learned brush planning and followed an airbrush-arm candidate. Robot motion and conventional control alone do not establish AI planning; physical hardware compatibility is untested.
The ToonComposer page returned only a title; adjacent primary animation sources and repository metadata remained available. No new result is inferred from the unreadable project shell.
Read LTX Foley guidance, which documents LTX-2.3 validation while 2.5 support remains in progress. Added audio restoration and stem guidance separately from generating scene-matched sound effects.

Read CoolChic, neural collage and LenslessMic, and completed StableCodec and LenslessMic guides. Perceptual similarity does not prove lossless reconstruction or a security property. The final catalog pass completed SNAC and Moshi/Mimi guides, retaining mono-codec and backend-specific limitations.
Read sound-object and audio-representation contexts and inspected brain2music’s offline script. AudioStellar’s GitLab page returned a loading shell; EEG sonification is not verified thought decoding.
Read Timeflux/MindDrawPlay contexts and inspected the existing EEG-to-spectrogram-to-Riffusion project. Hardware drivers and an end-to-end model-enabled entrypoint remain follow-up work.
Read Material Apprentice’s editable shader-graph workflow and reviewed agent/3D candidates. A procedural graph, model-generated texture and trained material estimator remain distinct workflows.
Read E2VID and lensless reconstruction and completed LenslessMic’s supplied-data route. Event sensors and lensless masks are physical requirements for acquisition, not implied by notebook access.
Read COrigami’s text-to-folding pipeline and its learned ranking/optimization stages. Digital paper-like appearance is not evidence of a physically realizable fold.
Read GardenDesigner’s agent-generated scene context. No new eligible tool with independently verified planting or site-design results was established in this bounded pass.
Read neural collage representations and reviewed stroke/halftone/palette-adjacent tools. Conventional mosaic optimization alone is not included as AI.
Read Visual Anagrams, Factorized Diffusion and Diffusion Illusions primary pages. Previously profiled unchanged tools are not presented again as new discoveries.

Read inverse-halftoning research and the current Deep Halftoning README. Reconstructed tonal detail is not laser/process safety or print fidelity, and its unreproducible paper metrics remain explicit.

New planned field: read Compositional Neural Painter and Stylized Neural Painting research, then reviewed MambaPainter, LearningToPaint and PaintTransformer software. Missing or conflicting licenses were held; available licensed implementations receive guides. A final query-result pass also found neural-painter notebooks, a watercolor GAN and a coordinate-to-color learning experiment; the neural-painter notebooks now have a complete guide, while watercolor and legacy coordinate-to-color code remain pending.

New planned field: read NeuralPreset’s paper and inspected palette-conditioning tools. NeuralPreset lacks a retrieved software license; the included palette workflow distinguishes conventional color processing from its separate AI generator.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Read the first 50 diffusion-search results and followed AudioSR, LongCat AudioDiT TTS and Foundation-1 node repositories into current README/license evidence. Two MIT audio integrations qualify for screening. The Foundation-1 wrapper LICENSE lookup failed and its README describes restricted model terms, so it is held for software-license clarification. Mirrors are not counted as distinct upstream tools.

The diffusion API request timed out; a supplemental neural query succeeded and returned 50 bounded results. Reviewed descriptions include neural colorization, archaeological image classification, speech bindings and many generic ML repositories or mirrors. No additional distinct tool received a complete current license review in this pass.

Read the neural project search and supplemental diffusion/audio pages. Generic ML and conventional audio entries are not automatically creative AI tools. This bounded pass did not establish another newly licensed, distinct application.

Read current PyPI JSON metadata for neutone-sdk 1.5.2 and the SDAI F-Droid listing. The PyPI HTML project page returned a challenge, so the successful JSON endpoint is distinguished from that failed page; registry license labels are not complete software-license reviews.
Read Neutone and QGIS primary pages, ComfyUI audio nodes and palette workflow documentation. Host requirements, external weights and optional cloud generation are separate from plugin source terms.

Fresh primary-page reads supplement all effective fields, including neural brushstrokes and color direction. SyncLight TLS failure and title-only/script-shell results from several sites remain explicit limitations.

Followed painting, relighting, neural compression, lensless audio and caustics papers into repository code and full software licenses. An MIT file in an otherwise empty NeRC repository is not a released implementation; conflicting painting terms are held.

Read Turkish microtonal OMR, Chinese/English creative tool documentation and the German INTEX textile case study. Language and popularity are not quality verdicts; model/data rights and platform limits remain explicit.

watchlist.name: Compositional Neural Painter
watchlist.reason: The complete software-license lookup returned 404; a published paper and repository do not establish an open-source grant.

watchlist.name: Stylized Neural Painting
watchlist.reason: The root CC0 license conflicts with the README statement that the work is licensed CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. The scope needs clarification before open-source inclusion.

watchlist.name: NeuralPreset
watchlist.reason: The paper describes a learned color-preset method, but a complete repository software license was not retrieved. The project-site page returned no substantive text.

watchlist.name: NeRC
watchlist.reason: The current repository tree contains only README and license, and the README says code will be released later. The caustics demo and dataset do not make an available application.

watchlist.name: GitLab ComfyUI Foundation-1
watchlist.reason: The README describes a concrete music workflow but LICENSE returned 404. Its model terms are restricted and do not establish the wrapper software grant.

watchlist.name: Open Airbrush Arm
watchlist.reason: The current README explicitly describes early planning, and the tree contains no firmware, software or motion-capture implementation. A build plan is not yet an executable AI painting tool.

watchlist.name: Uniscript MCP
watchlist.reason: The repository contains documentation and images for a paid remote service, with no implementation source. Its license explicitly covers documentation and associated files; this does not establish an open-source carousel-generation service.

watchlist.name: Avatar Motion Lab
watchlist.reason: The current tree contains only the license file and no README or application implementation. Repository description alone does not establish an available AI motion tool.

watchlist.name: Holo4D — model card with unavailable linked source
watchlist.reason: The current model card describes geometry-conditioned novel-view generation and claims released code. Its linked NIRVANALAN/Holo4D GitHub repository, README and license all returned 404 in this review; software availability and complete software license could not be established. Model metadata alone does not qualify an open-source tool.

watchlist.name: OpenDesign — nonstandard license wording
watchlist.reason: GitHub reports Apache-2.0, but a complete word comparison found edits to the trademark exception in section 6 and the support/liability wording in section 9. Held for license clarification; the SPDX label alone does not establish an unmodified recognized software grant.

watchlist.name: 3D Data Materials — simulated AI semantics kit
watchlist.reason: The inspected open-vocabulary semantics kit explicitly does not run SAM, CLIP or DINOv2: it simulates model outputs and performs conventional 3D fusion. A linked Depth-Anything reconstruction implementation is a separate repository. This tutorial collection is not counted as an additional verified AI tool.
